name: The Judas Factor
label: Revelation
lede: Rob Fish put The Judas Factor together right after Ressurection, fired his old guitarist inside three shows, and made two Revelation records that stop being hardcore halfway through. One early member now sits in New York City government.

eras.title: Five practices and a 7"
eras.text: After Ressurection, Fish had the whole band lined up before he asked his former guitarist to join: friends from Indecision, Ressurection's old bassist, and a Wreck-Age Records deal. They rehearsed a handful of times, recorded, and the first line-up was gone within the year.

years.h: Rob Fish builds a new band from Indecision and Ressurection
years.p: Fish brings in Pat and [[Justin Brannan|2cf0dcde-8417-46ff-96a9-74328669b417]] from Indecision, Ressurection's bassist Little Dave, and guitarist [[Chris Zusi|2a9965ad-0a98-4665-9bc0-aebec823fb44]], his bandmate in Ressurection. The band is already formed when Zusi is asked.
years.xp: "Rob had put the whole band together before he and Little Dave asked me to join," Zusi told No Echo. Three of the five had played in Ressurection; Pat and Justin came from Indecision.

years.h: The self-titled 7" comes out on Wreck-Age
years.p: Zusi plays guitar on the first Judas Factor record. Fish had the Wreck-Age Records deal arranged before the band had a rehearsal schedule.
years.xp: "I think we only practiced 5-8 times before we recorded the 7"," Zusi told No Echo.

years.h: Zusi is out after two or three shows
years.p: Zusi's description of how the band changed: he was fired after the first shows, and Brannan and Pat left soon after, heading in a different musical direction.
years.xp:
"After that I played the first two or three shows with the band and then they kicked me out!" Zusi told No Echo. He had played with Fish in Ressurection from 1991 to 1995 and went on to [[Floorpunch|8ecf80c2-d090-4cbd-97ec-0a0824301041]].

Of Fish, he said: "I think that he had a definite idea of where he wanted to take it."

eras.title: Two records on Revelation
eras.text: The Judas Factor made two Revelation records that sound little like late-'90s chug: one that changes genre in the middle, then an EP on green vinyl.

years.h: Ballads in Blue China goes soft in the middle
years.p: It opens with aggressive vocals and riffs, drops into indie rock midway, then goes heavy again. Twelve songs, including That Beautiful Old Victorian Bathtub.
years.xp:
Revelation catalog REV 78. The first vinyl pressing is 169 copies on red.

Impact Press, quoted on RevHQ: "The Judas Factor is a band you'll want to hear, with lyrics you need to read."

years.h: Kiss Suicide, 223 copies on opaque green
years.p: The second and last Revelation release, REV 92. The only vinyl pressing is that 223.

eras.title: From Indecision to City Hall
eras.text: Justin Brannan went on to the New York City Council, then a run for city comptroller.

years.cap: Justin Brannan, December 2017, weeks before he joined the NYC Council
years.src: Wikipedia: Justin Brannan · No Echo · Discogs
years.h: Brannan takes his seat on the NYC Council
years.p: Justin Brannan, of Indecision, [[Most Precious Blood|1f43313f-4855-4b5f-af16-90ab6ab8cf36]] and briefly The Judas Factor, represents Brooklyn's 43rd district starting January 1, 2018.
years.xp: He served through 2025 and moved to the 47th district in 2024. In the 2025 Democratic comptroller primary he took 41.28% in the final round to Mark Levine's 58.72%, finishing second.
